title: METEOR v8.0: evidence-weighted reaction selection reconciles enzyme prediction with growth feasibility
description:
Code and deposited results for the PSB 2027 submission METEOR: Evidence-weighted reaction selection reconciles enzyme prediction with growth feasibility.

METEOR takes a per-protein EC confidence matrix, aggregates it into reaction-level evidence, and selects a biomass-feasible reaction set from the ModelSEED universal database with a mixed-integer linear program, then maps the result back onto the protein score matrix through a bounded per-EC update that preserves protein ordering within each EC column. The cost grades each reaction by the confidence behind it rather than charging every reaction the same: a uniform penalty prunes by count regardless of evidence, whereas grading by confidence can retain evidence-supported redundant reactions and alternative routes while discouraging the weak tail and keeps the redundancy the evidence supports.

This is not weighted gap-filling. There is no thresholded draft: candidate reactions (reaction confidence >= 0.01, the medium, and a shared biomass-feasible skeleton) compete on one evidence-derived cost, followed by post-solve growth verification and, where needed, a parsimony repair, and the whole set is chosen in one optimisation.

The deposit carries the per-genome records behind every reported number, including the 108 MILP solutions the main-text tables are computed from, and three aggregation scripts that regenerate the published figures from the deposit alone.
